resale_co.name: Certificate of Compliance (exterior housing code and property area inspection on sale)
resale_co.issued_by: Borough of Oaklyn Administrative Office of Code Enforcement (Housing Code Department)
resale_co.valid_for: 90 days, provided the seller has not changed (2018 borough form)
requirements: Exterior housing code inspection and exterior property area inspection on every sale or resale
Sidewalks, walkways, driveways and driveway aprons made safe: no cracks, raised walkways or deteriorated concrete (asphalt or macadam for driveways only, not aprons or sidewalks)
Handrails where there are three or more steps; steps 30 inches above grade need a handrail on one side; 2 inch round handrails returned to post, with no more than 4 inch spindle spacing
Railings on porch or stoop perimeters that have none, with no more than 4 inch spindle spacing
Peeling, chipping or unpainted exterior surfaces scraped and painted
Broken window panes repaired
Open electrical splices or improperly installed fixtures corrected
Gutters and downspouts hooked up and in place
Any obvious hazardous and maintenance conditions
Repairs the Code Enforcement office finds necessary must be completed within 30 days of notice
Sump pump must not be connected to the sanitary sewer; Public Works inspects before settlement

fees.label: Housing code exterior inspection on sale (covers all inspections and reinspections)
fees.quote: A fee of $50 shall be paid to the Administrative Office of Code Enforcement upon the receipt of a request for a housing code exterior inspection.

resale_co.how_to_apply: Request the exterior inspection from the Code Enforcement office at Borough Hall, 500 White Horse Pike, Oaklyn, NJ 08107 (tel. 856-858-2457). The borough's Certificate of Compliance form (updated 10/10/18) asks for the settlement date, block and lot, contact person, property address and owner, and how to receive the repair letter and certificate (pick up, mail or fax). Confirm the current form and how to pay with Borough Hall, since the current borough website could not be read.

evidence.quote: It is hereby determined that an exterior housing code inspection and an exterior property area inspection, as defined in the BOCA National Property Maintenance Code/1996, shall be required on the sale and/or resale of all properties within the boundaries of the Borough of Oaklyn.
Such fees shall be paid only once and will include all costs for inspections; to include reinspection of any violations and the correction thereof.
Upon satisfactory inspection, the Administrative Office or Code Enforcement will issue a certificate of compliance relative to this housing code exterior inspection.
A Certificate of Compliance inspection is required upon the sale of all properties.
The Certificate is good for (90) days provided the seller has not changed.

resale_co.notes: The requirement and fee are in town code Chapter 101 (Property Maintenance), section 101-3, read in full through the ecode360 print view. The $50 fee on the 2018 borough form matches the code, so it is listed once. The 2018 Certificate of Compliance form is a scanned PDF on the borough's file host (the same host the current site uses for its New Resident Packet), so quotes were transcribed from the page images. It also listed old borough fire code fees ($60 to $160) and a fire extinguisher; those are superseded by the Regional Fire Prevention Alliance and are not reported as current. The current site (www.oaklyn-nj.net) is behind a bot challenge and loads content by script; no current resale page or email could be read. Rental units need a separate certificate of occupancy before each new tenant (section 101-5, $25 per unit); that is a rental program, not a resale requirement.

requirements: Smoke alarms by construction date: pre-1975 homes need 10-year sealed battery alarms on each level including the basement; newer homes need AC powered interconnected alarms per the era table on the form
Smoke alarms on every level, outside sleeping areas, and at the bottom of basement stairwells
All smoke alarms must be less than 10 years old; someone must take them down and check the date on the back, and undated alarms must be replaced
Low voltage (alarm company) fire alarm systems must be tested by an alarm contractor before the inspection, with the certification shown to the inspector
CO alarm outside of but within 10 feet of all sleeping areas if the home has a fuel burning appliance, fireplace or garage; CO alarms must be less than 7 years old
House numbers: Arabic numerals at least 3 inches tall, contrasting, mounted at least 60 inches above ground and visible from the street

Secondary power source warning label (wording like 'CAUTION MULTIPLE SOURCES OF POWER', not handwritten) within 18 inches of the main electrical panel and meter if there is a generator, solar panels or battery storage
Everything must be done before the inspector arrives; an adult (18+) must be present at the start of the time block
Oaklyn ordinance (2018 borough form): smoke alarms on every floor and in every bedroom; 10-year sealed battery alarms required since 1/1/19

authorities.name: Regional Fire Prevention Alliance (run by Barrington Borough)
authorities.area_served: Entire borough (the Alliance serves Barrington, Hi-Nella, Lawnside, Mt. Ephraim and Oaklyn)
authorities.lead_time: 14 or more business days before the change of occupant for the lowest fee; weekends, holidays and the settlement date do not count. Inspections are scheduled Monday to Friday, 9am to 2pm. Certificates are valid 6 months and are not transferable.

fees.label: Request received 14+ business days before change of occupant
fees.quote: 14+ business days prior to the change of occupant is $66.00.

fees.label: Request received 8-13 business days before
fees.quote: 8-13 business days prior to the change of occupant is $74.00.

fees.label: Request received 4-7 business days before
fees.quote: 4-7 business days prior to the change of occupant is $106.00.

fees.label: Request received 3 business days or less before
fees.quote: 3 business days or less notice prior to change of occupant is $171.00.

fees.label: Reinspection after a failed inspection
fees.quote: ALL FAILED INSPECTIONS WILL REQUIRED A $50.00 RE INSPECTION FEE.

fees.label: Penalty for change of ownership or occupancy without the certificate
fees.quote: the owner will be subject to a penalty of $500 per occurrence (N.J.A.C. 5:70-2.3).

authorities.how_to_apply: Fill out the Regional Fire Prevention Alliance smoke alarm certification application (fillable PDF) and email it to firealliance@barringtonboro.com, or print it and drop it in the mailbox at 205 Haines Avenue, Barrington, NJ 08007. Include a check or money order payable to 'Regional Fire Prevention Alliance'. Walk-in office hours are Tuesday to Friday, 8am to 2pm. Fees are non-refundable.

evidence.quote: The Regional Fire Prevention Alliance of Barrington, New Jersey serves the Municipalities of Barrington, Hi-Nella, Lawnside, Mt. Ephraim and Oaklyn.
Inspection is required per NJ Fire Code 5:70-2.3 for the selling, renting, or change of occupancy in one or two family homes.
CERTIFICATIONS ARE VALID FOR 6 MONTHS and are Non transferable. FEES ARE NON-REFUNDABLE.
A CHECK OR MONEY ORDER PAYABLE TO “REGIONAL FIRE PREVENTION ALLIANCE” MUST ACCOMPANY THIS APPLICATION.

LEAID: 0426-001 Oaklyn Boro SMOKE DETECTOR COMPLIANCE Name: Barrington Fire Prev Alliance Addr: 205 Haines Ave Barrington NJ 08007 Enf Auth. Municipal Fire Official Nicholas D'Alonzo Phone (856) 547-0991
Barrington Borough is the LEA for Hi Nella, Lawnside, Mt Ephraim and Oaklyn Boroughs.
A smoke detector inspection is required upon the sale or resale of all single family and two family dwellings within Oaklyn.

fire_cert.notes: The Regional Fire Prevention Alliance is a shared fire prevention bureau run out of Barrington Borough under a shared service agreement; it is not a fire district. Its November 2025 application covers smoke alarms, CO alarms and the secondary power source label (CSACMASPSIL) and does not list a fire extinguisher requirement, which matches the 2025 state change (P.L.2025, c.19); an older December 2022 version required a 2-A:10-BC extinguisher. The form only mentions extinguishers in a reminder to check for recalled devices. Office: 205 Haines Avenue, Barrington. Fire code questions: Fire Official Nick D'Alonzo, fireofficial@barringtonboro.com; the NJ DCA fire directory lists him at ndalonzo@barringtonboro.com, (856) 547-0991. Oaklyn's own 2018 form cites Ordinance 13-96 (Chapter 73) for the smoke detector inspection and requires detectors on every floor and in every bedroom; the Alliance's December 2022 packet also printed an Oaklyn-only rule (ordinance 75-10A(4)) for a smoke alarm inside each sleeping area. Confirm with the Alliance whether in-bedroom alarms are checked on Oaklyn sales.

other_items.label: Sump pump sewer connection inspection by Public Works
other_items.detail: Town code section 108-12 bars connecting sump pumps and similar discharges to the sanitary sewer; the borough form has a Public Works sign-off and says Public Works inspects before settlement (the form cites both 108-12 and 108-22).
